doc.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022

title: Music then and now; Ellington dates as second engineer
summary: Asked about today's car music, Hank says music is music and that he was second engineer on many fast-moving Ellington dates.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: What is your opinion, you’re driving down the street these days, the music that you hear coming out of some cars is very different from what you would have heard coming out of cars in the 1960s.

You bet. I think that we worked a lot better in the 60s. I mean we were, you know, our equipment has gotten better since the 60s but I don’t think that, you know music doesn’t change. Music is music. And whether you do a date with Duke Ellington in 1960 or you do a date with Duke Ellington now, the music is still there. You’ve just got to make it better. I mean I was a second engineer on a lot of Duke Ellington dates and boy they flew. You know you had to be real quick. You could turn around and say, “Give me that second chorus” and you’re trying to find where the second chorus was, and they’re all talking and drinking coffee.
